newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia welcomes Belarus political compromise.
newsitem.headline: Russia welcomes Belarus political compromise.

text.p: Russia welcomed on Friday the political compromise reached between the feuding president and parliament in Belarus and the Kremlin said Moscow had a key role in defusing the row.

"Without exaggeration you can say that this is a huge success, a genuine breakthrough in the search for a way out of the constitutional crisis in Belarus," Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.

He drew special attention to Yeltsin's telephone conversation with President Alexander Lukashenko on Thursday, which was followed by an urgent mission to Minsk led by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

The mission succeeded in persuading Lukashenko to accept that a referendum on expanding his powers, planned for Sunday, would not be legally binding. In return, the Belarus parliament agreed to drop impeachment proceedings against him.

"For we Russians it was extremely important that the Russian side, respecting the sovereignty of a fraternal republic and without interfering in its internal affairs, played a role in the search for a political compromise," Yastrzhembsky said.
"The personal contribution of President Yeltsin in working out the Russian position and bringing the two opposing sides in Belarus closer together is indisputable," he said.
He added that the diplomatic success of the Russian mission showed the "viability" of integration between the two countries, which formed a two-state "community" last April.
